classification_reasons: The instructions describe only the right foot stepping behind with a knee pull and a left arm held up. A carioca normally alternates sides while travelling laterally, so it is unclear whether the exercise is right-only, left-only, alternating or bilateral. Laterality changes which limb joints count.
The text does not say whether the exercise is counted in repetitions or timed, so input_mode cannot be set.

The two frames show a high knee on one side and a foot behind the body, but not the crossing step or the hip rotation and abduction/adduction path between them. The mix of hip flexion, abduction/adduction and rotation, and ankle work, is not determined by the instructions.
The text says the knee goes straight up and down and the feet do not turn. This conflicts somewhat with the lateral crossover travel of a standard carioca, so the variant is unclear.
No enum family cleanly fits a low-amplitude agility step. The choice among hip_flexion, lunge and jump_and_throw would be a guess, and it depends on whether the drill involves a flight phase.
questions_requiring_context: Is this a continuous alternating carioca (both legs stepping behind in turn, travelling sideways) or a single-side step-behind-and-knee-drive repeated on the right leg only?
Is the exercise prescribed in repetitions or in duration (time or distance)?
Is there a true crossover step with hip rotation while travelling laterally, or an in-place step with a straight vertical knee drive?
Is there a flight or hop phase, or is one foot always in contact with the ground?
